title: Python SDK service-specific behavior for ZIA: admin, AppTotal, browser control and smart isolation

prose.text: These are claims about the Python SDK's service helpers, not about ZIA. Each covers one behavior a reader would otherwise have to infer from the method signature.

prose.label: Browser control and Smart Browser Isolation.

admin-user-role-id.statement: The admin user create and update helpers turn a `role_id` keyword into `{"role": {"id": ...}}`. The docstring says `scope_entity_ids` need not be given when the admin scope is ORGANIZATION.

quotes: be provided if the admin user's scope is set to ``ORGANIZATION``.
**NOTE**: This param doesn't need to be provided if the admin user's scope is set to ``ORGANIZATION``.

convert-to-user-spec.statement: The API specification describes `POST /adminUsers/{userId}/convertToUser` as removing a user's admin privileges while keeping them as a regular user, as an alternative to DELETE, which removes the admin and also removes them as a user. It says the admin user's details are first obtained with `GET /users` and then sent in the convert request.

expect.description:
Removes admin privileges for a user while retaining them as a regular user of your organization in the ZIA Admin Portal. This can be used as an alternative to the DELETE /adminUsers/{userId} request, which deletes an admin and removes them as a user from the ZIA Admin Portal. To learn more, see Deleting ZIA Admins.

Before you can delete the admin privileges for a user, you need to obtain the admin user's ID and other information by using the GET /users request and then send the admin user details in the POST /adminUsers/{userId}/convertToUser request.

apptotal-submit-on-miss.statement: `get_app` on the AppTotal client searches the catalog by app ID; if the app is absent the call submits it for analysis, and a later call is needed to read the result.

quotes: Searches the AppTotal App Catalog by app ID. If the app exists in the catalog, the app's information is returned. If not, the app is submitted for analysis. After analysis is complete, a subsequent GET request is required to fetch the app's information.
evidence.after: def get_app(self, app_id: str, verbose: bool = False)

apptotal-result-cap.statement: The `search_app` and `app_views` docstrings state that at most 200 results are returned.

quotes: Note: The maximum number of results that are returned is 200.

browser-control-shared-endpoint.statement: The older `browser_control_settings` client and the newer `secure_browsing` client both read and write the same path `/browserControlSettings`; the Go `browser_control_settings` and `secure_browsing` packages use that path too.

quotes: ### New ZIA Endpoint - Browser Control Policy

smart-isolation-id-keys.statement: `update_smart_isolation` remaps ID lists with `transform_common_id_fields(reformat_params, ...)`, and `reformat_params` lists the keys `smart_isolation_user_ids` and `smart_isolation_group_ids` for that.

smart-isolation-doc-keys.statement: The `update_smart_isolation` docstring and its example name the keyword arguments `smart_isolation_users_ids` and `smart_isolation_groups_ids`.

quotes: smart_isolation_users_ids (list[str]): IDs of users for which the rule is applied.
smart_isolation_groups_ids (list[str]): IDs of groups for which the rule is applied.

dlp-web-rule-excludes-saas.statement: The web DLP rule client's docstrings say its get and list-lite calls exclude SaaS Security API DLP policy rules, and that its update is not applicable to them.

quotes: Returns a DLP policy rule, excluding SaaS Security API DLP policy rules.
Updates an existing DLP policy rule. Not applicable to SaaS Security API DLP policy rules.
Lists name and ID for all DLP policy rules, excluding SaaS Security API DLP policy rules

dedicated-ip-lite-only.statement: The Python dedicated IP gateway client defines `list_dedicated_ip_gw_lite`, which reads `/dedicatedIPGateways/lite`.

dedicated-ip-no-crud.statement: The Python dedicated IP gateway client has no get, add, update or delete method.
dedicated-ip-no-crud.conditions: The client file at the pinned SDK defines only the constructor and `list_dedicated_ip_gw_lite`; a quote cannot pin the absence of further methods in code, so this rests on reading the whole file.

smart-isolation-kwarg-names.summary: Keyword names for Smart Browser Isolation user and group scoping in the Python SDK

positions.says: The docstring and example for update_smart_isolation name the keywords smart_isolation_users_ids and smart_isolation_groups_ids.

quotes: smart_isolation_users_ids (list[str]): IDs of users for which the rule is applied.

positions.says: The shared ID-remapping list names smart_isolation_user_ids and smart_isolation_group_ids, so the documented spellings are not in it.

smart-isolation-kwarg-names.impact: A caller who follows the docstring may leave the user and group ID lists unwrapped, not in the {id: ...} shape the API takes; what the API does with the unwrapped keys is not shown. Read the rule back after the call instead of trusting the call result.
